patients.summary: Logistics coordinator with long-standing HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B on tenofovir, hypertension and vitamin D deficiency who joined in 2023. Intermittent tenofovir adherence and no HCC surveillance precede a December 2025 admission that finds a 4 cm hepatocellular carcinoma in decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis; he is listed for liver transplant in February 2026.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
51 y/o man new to the practice. Relocated here in June for a logistics coordinator job with a regional distributor. Prior primary care and hepatitis B care were out of state; records release signed today.

Hepatitis B: has known about it for many years, told it is the "e-antigen negative" kind. On tenofovir for years, prescribed by his old GI. Last liver labs he thinks were about a year ago. No abdominal pain, no jaundice, no itching, appetite fine. Wants a GI doctor closer to home.
BP: on amlodipine 5 mg, home readings he says are usually high 120s/low 80s. No headaches, no chest pain.
Vitamin D: low level found by prior PCP, on 2000 units a day.

Past surgical: inguinal hernia repair in spring 2017, uncomplicated.
Meds: tenofovir disoproxil 300 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily.
Allergies: none to medications.
Family: father had liver cancer and died at 71. Mother has type 2 diabetes. Older brother also has hepatitis B, followed where he lives.
Social: came to the US with his family as a young boy. Lives alone in an apartment. Has never used tobacco. Does not drink at all. No recreational drugs. Walks most evenings.

Exam: well appearing, no scleral icterus. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, no hepatosplenomegaly, healed groin scar. No edema. Skin without spider angiomata or jaundice.

Assessment/plan
1. Chronic hepatitis B on tenofovir: continue. Baseline CMP and CBC today. Referral to local GI to take over HBV management.
2. Hypertension: reasonable on amlodipine 5. Continue.
3. Vitamin D deficiency: level today on current dose.
4. Health maintenance: HCV and HIV screening today. A1c given mother's diabetes. Lipids. Tdap today, last one he can't recall. Colon screening to discuss at next visit once prior records are in. PHQ-2 negative.
Follow up in about 6 months, sooner once labs are back.

documents.title: Your Lab Results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Kenji, your labs are back. Kidney function, blood sugar, A1c and cholesterol all look good. Your blood counts are normal. Your liver enzyme ALT is a little above the normal range (58), which we see sometimes in hepatitis B; the new GI team will want to see this, and I've sent it along with the referral. Hepatitis C and HIV screens were negative. Vitamin D is 27, a bit below where I'd like it, but let's keep the same dose for now and recheck next year. Talk soon.

Inguinal hernia repair 2017 op note included. Influenza vaccines yearly. No colon cancer screening on file. Routed to PCP for review and filed under media.

documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Gastroenterology outpatient consultation
Date of visit: 12/08/2023
Referred by: primary care, for continuing management of chronic hepatitis B

Mr. Chen is a 52-year-old man with long-standing chronic hepatitis B, previously managed by a gastroenterologist in another state, on tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg daily. He presents to establish with our group. He is entirely asymptomatic: energy is good, no abdominal pain, no change in weight, no yellowing of the eyes, no pruritus, no dark urine.

Other history: hypertension on amlodipine 5 mg; vitamin D deficiency on cholecalciferol 2000 IU; remote inguinal hernia repair.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history notable for hepatocellular carcinoma in his father (died at 71) and chronic hepatitis B in an older brother. Mother with type 2 diabetes.
Social: abstains from alcohol, never smoker. Emigrated as a child.

Examination: alert, comfortable, anicteric. Abdomen soft and nontender without organomegaly or ascites. No stigmata of chronic liver disease. Remainder of exam within normal limits.

Data: ALT today 64 U/L, mildly above the reference range. Hepatitis B profile: surface antigen positive, surface antibody negative, core antibody positive (IgG), e antigen negative, e antibody positive, consistent with HBeAg-negative chronic infection.

Impression: HBeAg-negative chronic hepatitis B on tenofovir with mild ALT elevation.
Recommendations:
- Continue tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg once daily; reviewed the importance of taking it every day.
- Return to clinic in 12 months with labs.

NKDA. Medications at time of visit: tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily, cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily.

Attending gastroenterologist

Annual exam, 52M.

Meds: tenofovir disoproxil 300 daily, amlodipine 5 daily, D3 2000 units daily. NKDA.

PHQ-2 0.
Plan:
- HBV: tenofovir every day; set a phone alarm. ALT and CMP today, will forward to GI. GI annual visit due December.

RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Not feeling right
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Morning doc. I've been really worn out for a couple of months and my stomach keeps getting bigger even though I'm eating less. Pants are tight but I've lost weight on the scale. Coworker said my eyes look yellow. Can I come in?

documents.title: Re: Not feeling right

documents.body: Yes, today. Come at 11:30. If you get confused, vomit blood or have black stools before then, go straight to the emergency department.

documents.title: Same-Day Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Same-day visit for progressive tiredness, a swelling belly and weight loss.
HPI: 54M with chronic hepatitis B. About two months of fatigue that has steadily worsened, now leaving work early. Abdomen enlarging over the same period with early fullness. Down about 10 lb from his usual without trying (72.4 kg in August, 68.1 today). Coworkers noticed yellow eyes last week. Urine darker. No fever, no vomiting, no blood in stool, no black stools, no confusion.
On direct questioning he has been missing tenofovir doses on and off for months, more this fall when work got busy; the mail-order box sat unopened for weeks at a time. Never made the GI follow-up. No alcohol.
Exam: tired appearing, oriented, no asterixis. Scleral icterus and jaundiced skin. Abdomen distended, liver edge firm and palpable below the right costal margin, shifting dullness. No tenderness. No leg edema.
Assessment: new jaundice, ascites and hepatomegaly with weight loss in chronic HBV with interrupted antiviral therapy. Concern for decompensated liver disease and a liver tumor given the family history.
Plan: called the regional hospital gastroenterology service and spoke with the admitting gastroenterologist, who accepted him for direct admission this afternoon for imaging, labs and paracentesis. His brother is driving him there now. Told to bring his medicine bottles. Resume tenofovir today, do not skip. Will follow while inpatient.

conditions.label: Cirrhosis of liver due to chronic hepatitis B

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily
Take 1 tablet by mouth once daily in the morning

medications.reason: stopped with diuretic start in decompensated cirrhosis

reports.text: Complete abdominal ultrasound. Liver enlarged with a coarse echotexture. In the right hepatic lobe there is a solid mass measuring 4.0 cm with irregular margins. Gallbladder without stones or wall thickening. No intrahepatic or extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation; common bile duct normal caliber. Portal vein patent with hepatopetal flow. Moderate ascites. Kidneys normal in size without hydronephrosis. Pancreas partially obscured by bowel gas, visualized portions unremarkable. Aorta normal caliber.
reports.conclusion: 4 cm right hepatic lobe mass with irregular borders. Ascites. No gallstones or biliary dilatation.

reports.study: MRI abdomen with and without contrast
reports.text: Multiphase MRI of the liver with and without gadolinium. Nodular liver contour consistent with cirrhosis. Single 4.0 x 3.7 cm observation in the right hepatic lobe showing nonrim arterial phase hyperenhancement, nonperipheral washout on portal venous and delayed phases, and an enhancing capsule. No additional hepatic observations. No tumor in vein; portal and hepatic veins patent. Moderate ascites. Gallbladder, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys unremarkable. No abdominal lymphadenopathy.
reports.conclusion: LI-RADS 5 (definite HCC), single 4.0 cm right-lobe lesion, no tumor in vein. Cirrhotic liver with moderate ascites.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast for staging. Lungs clear without nodules or masses. No pleural effusion. No mediastinal or hilar lymphadenopathy. Heart size normal. No osseous lesions.
reports.conclusion: No evidence of thoracic metastatic disease.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Regional hospital, gastroenterology inpatient service
Admitted 12/15/2025 (direct admission from primary care). Discharged 12/19/2025.

Reason for admission: two months of worsening fatigue, enlarging abdomen and a 10-pound weight loss in a 54-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B who has taken tenofovir inconsistently.

On arrival: jaundiced, liver palpably enlarged, fluid wave present. Alert, no encephalopathy. Afebrile, hemodynamically stable.

Key data: AFP 800 ng/mL. ALT 90, AST 110, alkaline phosphatase 300 U/L, total bilirubin 3.2 mg/dL, albumin 2.8. INR 1.6. Sodium 134, creatinine 0.94. WBC 5.1, hemoglobin 12.9, platelets 98. HBV DNA 38,600 IU/mL.
Ultrasound: 4 cm irregular mass in the right lobe; no gallstones; bile ducts not dilated.
MRI liver 12/16: single 4.0 cm right lobe lesion meeting LI-RADS 5 criteria, no vascular invasion; cirrhotic liver; moderate ascites.
CT chest 12/17: no metastases.
Diagnostic paracentesis 12/16: high serum-ascites albumin gradient, consistent with portal hypertension; cell count without evidence of infection; culture no growth.

Diagnoses:
1. Hepatocellular carcinoma, single 4.0 cm lesion, within Milan criteria (imaging diagnosis, no biopsy).
2. Decompensated cirrhosis secondary to chronic hepatitis B, with ascites. Child-Pugh class B (9).
3. Chronic hepatitis B with viremia in the setting of interrupted tenofovir.
4. Hypertension.

Hospital course: started on spironolactone and furosemide with a 2 g sodium diet; weight and abdominal girth decreased, electrolytes and creatinine stable. Tenofovir resumed on admission with extensive adherence teaching. Amlodipine discontinued as the diuretics were started; blood pressure 110s-120s systolic off it. Case discussed at the multidisciplinary liver tumor conference; recommendation for referral to transplant hepatology for liver transplant evaluation. Referral sent to the transplant center.

Discharge medications:
- tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg by mouth daily (do not miss doses)
- spironolactone 100 mg by mouth daily (new)
- furosemide 40 mg by mouth every morning (new)
- cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily
STOPPED: amlodipine 5 mg.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Follow-up: primary care within 1 week with basic metabolic panel; transplant hepatology clinic, to be scheduled by the center. Return for fever, abdominal pain, confusion, bleeding or rapid weight gain.

Discharging gastroenterology attending

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen 4 days after discharge from the regional hospital GI service, with his older brother. No discharge summary in our system yet; history from patient, brother, his after-visit paperwork and the pharmacy fill list.
What he was told: liver cancer, about 4 cm, one spot, and cirrhosis from the hepatitis B with fluid in the belly. Fluid was tapped and was not infected. Being referred for a liver transplant evaluation.
Medicines per discharge sheet and pharmacy: tenofovir 300 mg daily, spironolactone 100 mg daily (new), furosemide 40 mg mornings (new), vitamin D 2000 units. Amlodipine stopped in hospital. He has been taking every dose; brother set up a pill box.
Feels a little less heavy, still tired. Urinating more. No confusion, no fever, no bleeding, no dizziness standing.
Exam: weight 66.4 kg, down from 68.1 a week ago. BP 112/70. Jaundiced. Abdomen less tense, mild shifting dullness. No asterixis. No edema.
A/P:
- HCC in HBV cirrhosis, transplant referral pending: center will call him; he has the number. Med list updated.
- Ascites on diuretics: BMP today. Low salt diet reviewed with brother. Daily weights; call if up more than 2 lb in a day or 5 in a week.
- Chronic HBV: tenofovir daily, no misses.
- HTN: off amlodipine, BP fine.
- PCV20 today given cirrhosis.
- Records request sent to hospital for full summary and imaging.
Recheck 6-8 weeks, sooner as needed.

documents.title: Transplant Hepatology Consultation
documents.author: transplant hepatology
documents.body:
Transplant hepatology, new patient evaluation
Visit date: 01/21/2026
Referred by: hospital gastroenterology service, after December 2025 admission
Copy to: primary care physician

History: 54-year-old man with chronic hepatitis B, previously on tenofovir with interrupted adherence, admitted in December with jaundice, ascites and weight loss. Workup there showed a single 4.0 cm LI-RADS 5 lesion in the right lobe with AFP 800, no vascular invasion and no extrahepatic disease on CT chest, in a cirrhotic liver. Discharged on diuretics.
Since discharge: energy slightly better, abdomen smaller, weight stable at home. Taking tenofovir daily without misses, confirmed by his brother who fills his pill organizer. No confusion, no GI bleeding, no fevers.
No alcohol ever. Never smoker. Works as a logistics coordinator, currently on reduced hours. Brother is his main support and transportation.
Medications: tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg daily, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily, amlodipine 5 mg daily (listed on referral; patient reports it was stopped). NKDA.
Exam: mildly icteric. Alert, no asterixis. Abdomen with small-volume ascites, nontender. No edema.
Labs today: total bilirubin 2.9, albumin 3.0, INR 1.5. AFP 760. HBV DNA 210 IU/mL, falling on consistent tenofovir.

Assessment: hepatocellular carcinoma within Milan criteria in decompensated hepatitis B cirrhosis, Child-Pugh B. He is an appropriate candidate for liver transplant evaluation.
Plan:
- Formal transplant evaluation begun: surgical, social work, nutrition and financial consultations to be scheduled; standard evaluation testing per protocol.
- Continue tenofovir 300 mg daily; adherence is essential before and after transplant.
- Continue spironolactone 100 mg and furosemide 40 mg; 2 g sodium diet.
- Repeat liver imaging and AFP every 3 months while waiting.
- We will update primary care with the committee decision.

Transplant hepatology attending

54M, HCC in hepatitis B cirrhosis, now listed for liver transplant.
Transplant hepatology letter from 1/21 received in February: Child-Pugh B, within Milan, evaluation started. He reports committee approval and listing on 2/18; no letter from the center about that yet.
How he is doing: energy fair, back to about 30 hours a week. Belly stable, no fullness to speak of. Weighs himself every morning, 145-146 lb. Not missing tenofovir, brother still checks the pill box. No confusion, sleep ok, no bleeding, no fever. Mood: worried at times but coping, PHQ-9 4.
Meds reconciled with bottles: tenofovir disoproxil 300 mg daily, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, vitamin D3 2000 units daily. Not on amlodipine since December. NKDA.
Exam: BP 110/68. Weight 66.0 kg. Mild scleral icterus. Lungs clear. Heart regular. Abdomen soft, no tense ascites, nontender. No asterixis. No ankle edema.
A/P
1. HCC, listed for transplant: care led by the center; imaging every 3 months there. Added transplant waiting list status to problem list.
2. Decompensated HBV cirrhosis with ascites: controlled on spironolactone/furosemide. BMP, hepatic panel, CBC today; results to the transplant team.
3. Chronic hepatitis B: tenofovir daily, adherence good now.
4. Hypertension: off medication, BP low-normal on diuretics. No antihypertensive needed.
5. Vitamin D deficiency: continue D3.
Follow up in about 6 months or sooner; he will keep us posted after each center visit.

documents.title: Transplant Hepatology Follow-up
documents.author: transplant hepatology
documents.body:
Transplant hepatology follow-up
Visit date: 05/20/2026
Copy to: primary care physician

Mr. Chen remains active on the liver transplant waiting list (listed 02/18/2026). Doing reasonably; working part time. Adherent to tenofovir. No encephalopathy, bleeding or infections since our last visit.
MRI 05/12: single right-lobe LI-RADS 5 lesion, 4.3 cm (from 4.0 cm), no new lesions, no vascular invasion; still within Milan criteria.
Labs: AFP 820 ng/mL. HBV DNA not detected. Total bilirubin 2.7, INR 1.5.
Medications: tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg daily, spironolactone 100 mg daily, furosemide 40 mg daily, cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily. NKDA.
Assessment: HCC within Milan in Child-Pugh B hepatitis B cirrhosis, on the waiting list. Viral suppression achieved.
Plan: no medication changes. Bridging locoregional therapy to be discussed at our multidisciplinary tumor board. Next imaging and AFP in 3 months.

Transplant hepatology
